Subject: Major latency/error spike hitting checkout (urgent)

Jonas / Laura / Ben,

We're seeing a sustained latency spike and intermittent 5xx errors across our checkout flow starting ~08:45 PT. Page loads are timing out for ~18% of requests and tokenization requests to your embeddings endpoint are failing intermittently. This is affecting order throughput and our CS team is receiving escalations.

Immediate asks: can Redwood confirm whether this is a config/deployment issue, what mitigation you have in flight, and whether we'll have a durable fix timeline? We need an exec-level readout this morning — our COO and SRE lead are briefed and want to join.

I've attached a short sample of our gateway logs and a curl snippet we've been running.

Thanks,
Carol

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Major latency/error spike hitting checkout (urgent) — initial findings and corrective actions

On Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:26:00 -07:00 jonas_weber@redwood.com wrote:
> Carol — thanks for the heads up and the log sample. We're triaging now.

Team, short update after the first 18 minutes of triage:
- Root cause signal: an unexpected surge of long-tail token sequences from CrossWalk's peak hours combined with a suboptimal kernel selection path on the current quantized variant. The runtime failed to route a subset of requests to the fallback model variant quickly enough, resulting in queueing and transient OOMs on two nodes.
- Immediate mitigations performed (09:33–09:40 PT):
  * Forced failover of traffic off the two impacted nodes; replaced with spare capacity.
  * Hot-prefix KV priming run initiated by Grace (reduced cold-start token overhead).
  * Short-ttl cache bump on embeddings for common checkout prefixes.
- Impact: error rate returned to baseline by ~09:52 PT, median p95 latency improved from 2.4s -> 520ms for affected routes. Overall throughput stabilized but we need a durable fix for kernel selection under these long-tail payload distributions.

I'm attaching the incident timeline and a draft RCA with recommended corrective actions. Key follow-ups I recommend we own and track:
1) Runtime kernel selector: add a preflight that routes very long sequences to the non-quantized variant when peak length probability > 0.65. (Owner: ben_carter)
2) Autoscaler gap: ensure spare-node buffer is available for predictable peaks of this class — add new reserve policy. (Owner: grace_oconnor)
3) Model variant priming: proactive warmers for customer checkout prefixes at known peak windows. (Owner: marissa_cole)
4) Post-incident quality: define regression test in CI for token length distribution and kernel selector logic. (Owner: laura_bennett)

Attachments: crosswalk_rca_draft.pdf; incident_timeline.csv; mitigation_playbook_v1.xlsx

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Runtime Reliability | Redwood Inference

Subject: CrossWalk — final RCA delivered, remediation tally, and weekly sync cadence

Folks — closing the loop and capturing the committed runbook. Apologies for the longer delivery window; the team wanted to validate the kernel-selector patch under staging load.

Executive summary (one-liner): A long-tail token distribution during CrossWalk's peak caused the runtime to choose a quantized execution path that under-provisioned memory for a subset of requests, producing queueing and transient OOMs; mitigations stabilized traffic and we've scheduled a staged runtime change to avoid recurrence.

Remediation tally (owners and ETA):
- Ben Carter — kernel-selector enhancement; toggle + hotfix candidate by 2027-07-07, staged rollout to 10% traffic 2027-07-09, full rollout 2027-07-14. Risk: low/medium (requires canary memory metrics).
- Grace O'Connor — reserve-node autoscaler policy; policy implemented 2027-06-30; monitoring dashboard added. Risk: low.
- Marissa Cole — proactive model warmers for CrossWalk prefixes; initial warmers live 2027-07-02, extended schedule by 2027-07-10. Risk: operational overhead.
- Laura Bennett — CI regression test for token-length and selector logic; PR and pipeline test by 2027-07-06. Risk: low.

Operational commitments:
- Weekly status sync with CrossWalk (owner: Laura) every Tue 09:00 PT starting 2027-07-06; invite sent.
- Credit evaluation: commerce team to propose credit estimate by 2027-07-05 (cc'd finance in separate thread).
- Post-rollout verification window: 30 days of elevated telemetry monitoring; automatic rollback criteria defined in the associated runbook.
